dedupe_keys.name: polish flood hazard and flood risk maps isok hydroportal wody polskie

description: The Hydroportal of the ISOK system (Informatyczny System Osłony Kraju) is the public map portal of Polish Waters (Wody Polskie) for flood risk, drought and water management plans in Poland. It publishes the preliminary flood risk assessment, flood hazard maps showing water depths for floods with probabilities of 10%, 1% and 0.2% a year, flood risk maps, flood risk management plans, river basin management plans, the plan against drought effects, the national urban wastewater treatment programme and a layer of other water management facilities. Updated and new hazard and risk maps of the second planning cycle were made public on 22 October 2020 under the Water Law, in a cartographic PDF version and a vector version in the map modules. Access is free and open, WMS services feed a Wody Polskie QGIS plugin, but no licence is stated for the map data. Caveats: the maps cover only reaches and coasts designated as at significant risk, a map review under the EU Floods Directive is due, the 2024 flood postdates the 2020 maps, and WMS endpoints were not opened. Simulation uses: flood depth grids by return period for exposure of water, energy and transport assets, risk-based emergency planning, drought planning for water supply and irrigation, and locating wastewater treatment plants in flood zones. Related record: the Dutch LIWO flood layers (data-netherlands-liwo-flood-information) are a comparable national flood map service.
